Sub-tropical summer zenith — sun at 82-degree vertical angle, shadows punched directly beneath every boulder, overhang, and canopy cluster in hard-edged black at near-zero length, open ground blazing white-yellow at peak neutral color temperature, coastal shallows burning white-turquoise at maximum chromatic saturation, every exposed surface stripped to its rawest chromatic intensity, no atmospheric scattering to soften any edge.

Sun-shaft piercing storm gap — ragged cloud-break admitting a single column of warm amber-white light onto a 200-meter patch of valley floor, surrounding terrain sunk in deep charcoal-violet storm shadow, the illuminated patch blazing against the darkened plain at extreme tonal contrast, shaft edges defined by volumetric moisture scatter showing visible amber-gold crepuscular beam, cloud ceiling above burning dull copper at the break margin.
